probe: What is the consistency strength of the existence of a (strongly) inaccessible cardinal, expressed in terms of ZFC?
expected_answer: Strictly greater than ZFC: if ZFC + 'there exists an inaccessible cardinal kappa' is consistent, then V_kappa is a model of ZFC, so by the Second Incompleteness Theorem ZFC alone cannot prove the consistency of an inaccessible cardinal. Equivalently, an inaccessible cardinal kappa yields a transitive set model of ZFC. (Standard result; cf. Kanamori, 'The Higher Infinite', 2nd ed. 2003, Proposition 1.2.)
verification_method: direct citation; standard textbook result (Kanamori 2003, Jech 2003)
anti_gravitational_well_note: Phrased as 'can ZFC prove X?' the substrate-grade reframing is: inaccessibility implies a set model of ZFC, hence Con(ZFC), hence by Goedel-2 it is strictly above ZFC in interpretability strength. The well to avoid is hand-waving 'just past ZFC' — the precise statement is V_kappa models ZFC.

probe: State the Kunen inconsistency theorem and identify the year and journal of the original proof.
expected_answer: Theorem (Kunen 1971): In ZFC, there is no nontrivial elementary embedding j: V -> V of the universe into itself. Equivalently, Reinhardt cardinals are inconsistent with ZFC. Original proof: Kenneth Kunen, 'Elementary embeddings and infinitary combinatorics', Journal of Symbolic Logic 36 (1971), pp. 407-413. The proof uses Erdos-Hajnal-style coloring on j''lambda for lambda the supremum of the critical sequence; Kunen formulated it in Morse-Kelley but the argument adapts to ZFC + replacement for j-formulas.
verification_method: direct citation; verified via Wikipedia 'Kunen's inconsistency theorem' and Kanamori (2003) Sec. 23
anti_gravitational_well_note: The well: confusing 'no Reinhardt in ZFC' with 'no Reinhardt in ZF'. The latter is open. Substrate-grade answer specifies the use of choice (j''lambda is the obstruction) and that ZF-only consistency of a Reinhardt is unresolved.

probe: Who proved the consistency of Martin's Maximum (MM), from what large-cardinal hypothesis, and where was it published?
expected_answer: Foreman, Magidor, and Shelah (1988) proved that if there exists a supercompact cardinal, then there is a forcing extension in which Martin's Maximum holds. Reference: M. Foreman, M. Magidor, S. Shelah, 'Martin's Maximum, saturated ideals, and non-regular ultrafilters. Part I', Annals of Mathematics (2) 127 (1988), pp. 1-47 (with corrigendum vol. 129 (1989), p. 651).
verification_method: direct citation; verified via Annals of Mathematics archive and Wikipedia 'Martin's maximum'
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating 'MM is consistent relative to a large cardinal' without naming supercompact specifically. Lower bound is also relevant: MM implies AD^{L(R)}, hence consistency strength is at least omega Woodin cardinals; the gap between supercompact upper bound and omega Woodins lower bound is part of the substrate-grade picture.

probe: State Silver's theorem (1974) on the singular cardinals problem.
expected_answer: Silver's Theorem (Silver 1975, 'On the singular cardinals problem', Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Vancouver 1974, pp. 265-268): If kappa is a singular cardinal of uncountable cofinality and the GCH holds below kappa (i.e., 2^lambda = lambda^+ for all infinite cardinals lambda < kappa), then 2^kappa = kappa^+. In particular, GCH cannot first fail at a singular cardinal of uncountable cofinality such as aleph_{omega_1}.
verification_method: direct citation; standard result, in Jech 2003 Theorem 8.13
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating the theorem only for GCH below, missing the SCH-style strengthening (Silver actually proved the stronger statement for 2^kappa from the corresponding hypothesis on 2^lambda). Substrate-grade: distinguish original generic-ultrapower proof from later combinatorial Baumgartner-Prikry proof.

probe: What is the Whitehead problem, and who proved its independence from ZFC?
expected_answer: Whitehead's problem asks whether every abelian group A with Ext^1(A, Z) = 0 is free. Saharon Shelah proved its independence from ZFC: in 'Infinite Abelian Groups, Whitehead Problem and Some Constructions', Israel Journal of Mathematics 18 (1974), pp. 243-256, he showed (a) under V = L every Whitehead group is free, and (b) under MA + not-CH there exists a non-free Whitehead group of cardinality aleph_1. This was the first major result outside set theory shown to be independent of ZFC.
verification_method: direct citation; verified via Wikipedia 'Whitehead problem' and Israel J. Math archive
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: 'Whitehead is independent of ZFC' — the substrate-grade answer must specify both directions (V=L gives free, MA+not-CH gives non-free) because each direction is an independent set-theoretic technique. Also note Shelah later (1977) extended to CH alone.

probe: Define a Polish space and state the characterization of Borel sets as continuous images / one-to-one continuous images of Polish spaces.
expected_answer: A Polish space is a separable, completely metrizable topological space. The characterization (Lusin-Suslin theorem; cf. Kechris, 'Classical Descriptive Set Theory', Springer GTM 156, 1995, Theorem 15.1): in a Polish space X, a set B is Borel iff B is the injective continuous image of a closed subset of Baire space N = N^omega (equivalently, of some Polish space). Without injectivity the analytic (Sigma^1_1) sets are obtained, which strictly extend Borel.
verification_method: direct citation; Kechris 1995 is the canonical reference
source: Kechris, Classical Descriptive Set Theory (1995), Theorem 15.1
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: confusing analytic (continuous image, drop injectivity) with Borel (continuous injective image). Substrate-grade: emphasize the injectivity is the key, and that this is the Lusin-Suslin theorem, not just 'a definition'.

probe: Define Martin's Axiom (MA) and state Solovay-Tennenbaum's consistency theorem.
expected_answer: MA(kappa): for every ccc partial order P and every family of fewer than kappa^+ dense subsets of P, there is a filter meeting all of them. MA is the assertion that MA(kappa) holds for every kappa < 2^{aleph_0}. Solovay-Tennenbaum (R. M. Solovay and S. Tennenbaum, 'Iterated Cohen extensions and Souslin's problem', Annals of Mathematics (2) 94 (1971), pp. 201-245) showed that ZFC + MA + 2^{aleph_0} = kappa is consistent for any regular kappa >= aleph_2, by introducing finite-support iteration of ccc forcing. In particular MA + not-CH is consistent.
verification_method: direct citation; standard, see Kunen 'Set Theory' (2011), Ch. III
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating MA without the cardinal parameter, or omitting that the iteration must be finite-support ccc (countable-support breaks ccc preservation). Substrate-grade flags the iteration technology as the main contribution.

probe: What is the exact consistency strength of the failure of the Singular Cardinals Hypothesis (SCH)?
expected_answer: Equiconsistent with the existence of a measurable cardinal kappa with Mitchell order o(kappa) = kappa^{++}. Upper bound: Gitik (M. Gitik, 'The negation of the singular cardinals hypothesis from o(kappa) = kappa^{++}', Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 43 (1989), pp. 209-234), improving Magidor 1977 (which used a supercompact). Lower bound: Gitik (M. Gitik, 'The strength of the failure of the singular cardinals hypothesis', Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 51 (1991), pp. 215-240), using the Mitchell core model. Mitchell's review (JSL 56 (1991), p. 1135) records the equiconsistency.
verification_method: direct citation; verified via Wikipedia 'Singular cardinals hypothesis' and Gitik publication list
source: Gitik 1989/1991 (APAL 43, APAL 51); Mitchell core-model lower bound
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: answering 'measurable cardinal' without the Mitchell-order specification o(kappa)=kappa^{++}. A bare measurable is far too weak (it does not give failure of SCH). Substrate-grade: name the Mitchell rank and split upper/lower bounds.

probe: State Shelah's PCF bound on 2^{aleph_omega} when aleph_omega is a strong limit.
expected_answer: Shelah's Theorem (S. Shelah, 'Cardinal Arithmetic', Oxford Logic Guides 29, Clarendon Press 1994; original announcement Shelah 1989/1990): if aleph_omega is a strong limit (i.e., 2^{aleph_n} < aleph_omega for all n < omega), then 2^{aleph_omega} < aleph_{omega_4}. More generally, if A is an interval of regular cardinals, then |pcf(A)| < |A|^{+4}. The bound aleph_{omega_4} is provable in ZFC; whether aleph_{omega_1} suffices is open.
verification_method: direct citation; Shelah 'Cardinal Arithmetic' 1994, also Wikipedia 'PCF theory'
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating the bound as 'aleph_{omega_1}' (the conjectured optimal bound) rather than the actually proved aleph_{omega_4}. Substrate-grade distinguishes proved-in-ZFC from open.

probe: What does the Proper Forcing Axiom (PFA) imply about 2^{aleph_0}, and what is its consistency strength upper bound?
expected_answer: PFA implies 2^{aleph_0} = aleph_2 (Veličković 1992, 'Forcing and complete embeddings', and earlier Todorčević's reflection arguments; canonical reference: Bekkali, 'Topics in Set Theory', LNM 1476, 1991). Consistency upper bound: PFA is consistent relative to a supercompact cardinal (Baumgartner; cf. J. Baumgartner, 'Applications of the Proper Forcing Axiom', in Handbook of Set-Theoretic Topology, North-Holland 1984, pp. 913-959). The exact consistency strength is open but is known to be at least many Woodin cardinals (Schimmerling, Steel).
verification_method: direct citation; standard, Bekkali 1991 / Baumgartner Handbook 1984
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: 'PFA implies CH fails' is too weak — PFA pins 2^{aleph_0} exactly to aleph_2. Substrate-grade: distinguish upper bound (supercompact) from the still-open exact strength.

probe: State Jensen's Covering Lemma for L and one of its arithmetical consequences.
expected_answer: Jensen's Covering Lemma (R. B. Jensen, circulated 1974; published proof in Devlin-Jensen 'Marginalia to a theorem of Silver', in Logic Conference Kiel 1974, LNM 499, 1975, pp. 115-142): If 0^# does not exist, then for every uncountable set X of ordinals there is a Y in L with X subset Y and |Y| = |X|. Consequence: if 0^# does not exist, then for every singular cardinal kappa, kappa is singular in L and (kappa^+)^L = kappa^+; in particular SCH holds. Equivalently, the failure of SCH (or 'kappa^+ of L below kappa^+') implies 0^# exists.
verification_method: direct citation; canonical reference Devlin-Jensen 1975, LNM 499; also Jech 2003 Ch. 18
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating Covering Lemma without a consequence (so the answer is unfalsifiable). Substrate-grade: pair the lemma with the SCH-implication, which is the anti-large-cardinal teeth of the result.

probe: State the precise consistency-strength equiconsistency for ZF + AD (Axiom of Determinacy).
expected_answer: ZF + AD is equiconsistent with ZFC + 'there exist infinitely many Woodin cardinals'. Upper bound (AD^{L(R)} from omega Woodin + measurable above): Martin-Steel-Woodin, '(Projective) determinacy from omega Woodin cardinals' (cf. D. A. Martin and J. R. Steel, 'A proof of projective determinacy', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 2 (1989), pp. 71-125, and Woodin's extension to AD^{L(R)}). Lower bound: Woodin (using core-model induction techniques). Canonical exposition: Steel, 'The derived model theorem', and Larson, 'The Stationary Tower' (2004).
verification_method: direct citation; Martin-Steel 1989 JAMS; Woodin lower bound, see Kanamori 2003 Sec. 32
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: saying 'AD requires large cardinals' without giving the precise omega-Woodin equiconsistency. Substrate-grade splits projective determinacy (n+1 Woodins suffice for boldface Pi^1_{n+1}) from full AD^{L(R)} (omega Woodins + measurable above).

probe: What is the Suslin Hypothesis (SH), and what is its status with respect to ZFC?
expected_answer: Suslin Hypothesis (SH): every ccc dense linear order without endpoints that is order-complete is isomorphic to (R, <). Equivalently, there is no Suslin tree (a tree of height omega_1 with no uncountable chain or antichain). Independence: (a) Tennenbaum (1968, 'Souslin's problem', Proc. Nat. Acad. Sci. 59:60-63) and Jech (1967, 'Non-provability of Souslin's hypothesis', Comment. Math. Univ. Carolinae 8:291-305) showed Con(ZFC) implies Con(ZFC + not-SH) by forcing a Suslin tree. (b) Solovay-Tennenbaum 1971 (Ann. Math. 94:201-245) showed Con(ZFC) implies Con(ZFC + MA + not-CH), and MA + not-CH implies SH. Hence SH is independent of ZFC; in fact diamond (V=L) implies a Suslin tree exists (Jensen 1972).
verification_method: direct citation; standard, see Jech 2003 Ch. 9 and Kunen 2011 Ch. III
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: 'SH is independent of ZFC' — needs both directions named with their forcings/diamond construction. Substrate-grade: name the Suslin-tree construction from diamond (Jensen) and the SH side from MA+not-CH.

probe: State the Mansfield-Solovay theorem on Sigma^1_2 sets and 0^#.
expected_answer: Mansfield-Solovay Theorem: every Sigma^1_2 set of reals either is contained in L or has a perfect subset. Equivalently, if every real is in L, then every Sigma^1_2 set is either countable or contains a perfect set. Reference: R. B. Mansfield, 'Perfect subsets of definable sets of real numbers', Pacific J. Math. 35 (1970), pp. 451-457; see also Moschovakis, 'Descriptive Set Theory', 2nd ed. (2009), Theorem 4F.1. Consequence: if 0^# exists then there is a Pi^1_2 singleton not in L (Solovay), separating Sigma^1_2-perfect-set from arbitrary Sigma^1_2 behavior.
verification_method: direct citation; Mansfield 1970 Pacific J. Math.; Moschovakis 2009 textbook
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: confusing the Mansfield-Solovay theorem (Sigma^1_2-dichotomy with L) with the simpler perfect-set theorem for analytic sets (Suslin). Substrate-grade: emphasize the L vs. perfect dichotomy as the substantive content.

probe: State the Asperó-Schindler theorem (2021) on Martin's Maximum^{++} and Woodin's axiom (*).
expected_answer: Theorem (D. Asperó and R. Schindler, 'Martin's Maximum^{++} implies Woodin's axiom (*)', Annals of Mathematics (2) 193 (2021), no. 3, pp. 793-835): MM^{++} (Martin's Maximum^{++}) implies Woodin's axiom (*) (the P_max axiom asserting that L(R) satisfies AD and that H_{omega_2} is a generic extension of L(R) by Woodin's P_max forcing). This resolves the long-standing question of the relationship between the two main families of axioms deciding the Sigma^2_1 theory of H_{omega_2}, both of which independently imply 2^{aleph_0} = aleph_2.
verification_method: direct citation; verified via Annals of Mathematics 2021 vol. 193 issue 3 and arXiv:1906.10213
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating 'MM implies (*)' (insufficient — the result requires MM^{++}, the strengthening with stationary preservation in H_{omega_2}). Substrate-grade pinpoints the ++ strengthening and identifies what (*) actually asserts at H_{omega_2}.

probe: State Mitchell's theorem on the Mitchell order on normal measures and the cardinality of o(kappa).
expected_answer: The Mitchell order ◁ on normal measures on a measurable cardinal kappa is defined by mu ◁ nu iff mu in Ult(V, nu) (i.e., mu lies in the ultrapower by nu). Mitchell (W. Mitchell, 'Sets constructible from sequences of ultrafilters', Journal of Symbolic Logic 39 (1974), pp. 57-66) showed that ◁ is well-founded. The Mitchell rank o(kappa) is the rank of ◁ on normal measures on kappa; o(kappa) <= (2^kappa)^+ (in fact <= kappa^{++} when V = K^{Mitchell}). The order is a strict partial order, and o(kappa) calibrates a sub-hierarchy strictly below 'measurable of order o(kappa) = (2^kappa)^+'.
verification_method: direct citation; Mitchell 1974 JSL; standard exposition Kanamori 2003 Sec. 19
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating Mitchell order without the well-foundedness theorem (which is the substantive content). Substrate-grade pairs the definition with the bound o(kappa) <= (2^kappa)^+ and the inner-model context where it is sharp.

probe: Under AD, what is the order type of the Wadge hierarchy on Baire space, and who proved its well-foundedness and semi-linearity?
expected_answer: Under AD: (1) Wadge's Lemma (W. Wadge, PhD thesis, Berkeley 1983; results from late 1960s/early 1970s): for any A, B ⊆ omega^omega, either A <_W B or omega^omega \ B <_W A (semi-linear ordering of Wadge degrees). (2) Martin's well-foundedness theorem (D. A. Martin, unpublished; cf. A. S. Kechris, 'Wadge degrees and projective ordinals', also exposition in Kanamori 2003 Sec. 30): the Wadge ordering modulo complementation is well-founded. The well-ordered length, after identifying each set with its complement, equals Theta = sup{alpha : alpha is the order type of a prewellordering of R}.
verification_method: direct citation; Wadge 1983 thesis; Martin unpublished proof, see Kechris 'Wadge degrees and projective ordinals'
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating 'Wadge degrees are well-ordered' (false — they are well-ordered only after identifying sets with complements; raw Wadge order has antichains of size 2). Substrate-grade specifies the modding out, names Martin for well-foundedness and Wadge for semi-linearity, and gives length Theta.

probe: Define NIP (dependent) and NSOP_n in Shelah's classification, and state the inclusion between simple, NIP, and NSOP theories.
expected_answer: NIP (no independence property; equivalently 'dependent'): a complete theory T is NIP if no formula phi(x; y) has the independence property — i.e., there are no a_i and b_J such that phi(a_i; b_J) iff i in J for all finite J ⊆ omega (S. Shelah, 'Stability, the f.c.p., and superstability', Annals of Mathematical Logic 3 (1971), pp. 271-362; canonical text: Shelah, 'Classification Theory', North-Holland 1990). NSOP_n: T omits the n-strong order property — there is no definable relation that orders an infinite set with a specific n-cycle obstruction (Shelah, 'Toward classifying unstable theories', Annals of Pure and Applied Logic 80 (1996), pp. 229-255). Inclusions among complete theories: stable ⊊ simple ⊊ NSOP_3 ⊊ NSOP_4 ⊊ ... ⊊ NSOP, and orthogonally stable ⊊ NIP. Simple ∩ NIP = stable (Shelah).
verification_method: direct citation; Shelah 1971 AML; Shelah 1996 APAL; standard text Shelah Classification Theory (1990)
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: confusing NIP with NSOP (different dividing lines) or stating 'NIP = stable' (false; NIP is strictly weaker — e.g., RCF and ACVF are NIP but unstable). Substrate-grade names the formula-level independence property and the simple-NIP-stable triangle.

probe: What is the Kurepa Hypothesis, and what is its consistency strength relative to ZFC?
expected_answer: Kurepa Hypothesis (KH): there exists a Kurepa tree — a tree of height omega_1 with each level countable and at least aleph_2 uncountable branches. Status: (a) KH is consistent with ZFC (it holds in L, by Solovay; cf. K. Devlin 'Aspects of Constructibility', LNM 354, 1973). (b) The negation of KH (¬KH) is equiconsistent with the existence of an inaccessible cardinal (Silver 1971, unpublished; exposition: J. Silver, 'The independence of Kurepa's conjecture and two-cardinal conjectures in model theory', in Axiomatic Set Theory, Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. XIII Part I, AMS 1971, pp. 383-390). Specifically, in the Levy collapse Coll(omega_1, < kappa) of an inaccessible kappa, omega_2 of the extension is inaccessible in L, blocking Kurepa trees.
verification_method: direct citation; Silver 1971 PSPM XIII Part I; Devlin LNM 354 1973
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: 'KH is independent of ZFC' (true but incomplete) — the substrate-grade fact is that ¬KH is equiconsistent with an inaccessible, while KH itself is consistent outright (V=L). The asymmetry is the load-bearing content.

probe: State Woodin's theorem on the structure of L(R) under AD^{L(R)} (the 'derived model theorem' / generation of AD^{L(R)} from omega Woodin cardinals).
expected_answer: Theorem (W. H. Woodin; canonical exposition: J. Steel, 'The derived model theorem', in Logic Colloquium 2006, Lecture Notes in Logic 32, ASL/Cambridge 2009, pp. 280-327; also Woodin, 'The Axiom of Determinacy, Forcing Axioms, and the Nonstationary Ideal', De Gruyter 1999/2010): If there are omega Woodin cardinals with a measurable above their supremum lambda, then in V[G] for G generic for Coll(omega, < lambda), the derived model D = L(R*, Hom*) (where R* is the symmetric reals and Hom* the symmetric homogeneously Suslin sets) satisfies AD^+ and AD^{L(R)} holds in D. Equiconsistency: Con(ZFC + omega Woodin cardinals) <-> Con(ZF + AD).
verification_method: direct citation; Steel 2009 LNL 32; Woodin De Gruyter 1999/2010 monograph
source: Woodin (derived model theorem); Steel 2009 LNL 32 exposition
anti_gravitational_well_note: Well: stating 'omega Woodins gives AD' without the derived-model construction or the symmetric-collapse setup. Substrate-grade names the symmetric reals R*, the homogeneously Suslin sets Hom*, the Coll(omega, < lambda) generic, and that AD^+ (not just AD) holds in the derived model.
